Gasparro</a>'s obverse design (left) and reverse design (right) of the Presidential Medal of Appreciation award during Eisenhower's official visit to the State of Hawaii from June 20 to 25, 1960</div></div></div></div>
<p>Eisenhower founded <a href="/wiki/People_to_People_International" title="People to People International">People to People International</a> in 1956, based on his belief that citizen interaction would promote cultural interaction and <a href="/wiki/World_peace" title="World peace">world peace</a>. The program includes a <a href="/wiki/People_to_People_Student_Ambassadors" class="mw-redirect" title="People to People Student Ambassadors">student ambassador component</a>, which sends American youth on educational trips to other countries.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During his second term as president, Eisenhower distinctively preserved his presidential gratitude by awarding individuals a special memento. This memento was a series of specially designed U.S. Mint presidential appreciation medals. Eisenhower presented the medal as an expression of his appreciation and the medal is a keepsake reminder for the recipient.<sup id="cite_ref-Gomez_335-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gomez-335">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The development of the appreciation medals was initiated by the White House and executed by the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Mint" title="United States Mint">United States Mint</a>, through the <a href="/wiki/Philadelphia_Mint" title="Philadelphia Mint">Philadelphia Mint</a>. The medals were struck from September 1958 through October 1960. A total of twenty designs are cataloged with a total mintage of 9,858. Each of the designs incorporates the text "with appreciation" or "with personal and official gratitude" accompanied with Eisenhower's initials "D.D.E." or facsimile signature. The designs also incorporate locations, dates and significant events. Prior to the end of his second term as president, 1,451 medals were turned in to the Bureau of the Mint and destroyed.<sup id="cite_ref-Gomez_335-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gomez-335">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup> The Eisenhower appreciation medals are part of the Presidential Medal of Appreciation Award Medal Series.<sup id="cite_ref-Gomez_335-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gomez-335">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Tributes_and_memorials">Tributes and memorials</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/List_of_memorials_to_Dwight_D._Eisenhower" title="List of memorials to Dwight D. Eisenhower">List of memorials to Dwight D. Eisenhower</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Eisenhower_Interstate_System_IMG_4192.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Eisenhower_Interstate_System_IMG_4192.JPG/220px-Eisenhower_Interstate_System_IMG_4192.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Eisenhower_Interstate_System_IMG_4192.JPG/330px-Eisenhower_Interstate_System_IMG_4192.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Eisenhower_Interstate_System_IMG_4192.JPG/440px-Eisenhower_Interstate_System_IMG_4192.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="3000" /></a><figcaption>Eisenhower Interstate System sign south of <a href="/wiki/San_Antonio" title="San Antonio">San Antonio</a>, Texas</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:1974S_Eisenhower_Obverse.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/1974S_Eisenhower_Obverse.jpg/220px-1974S_Eisenhower_Obverse.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="219" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/1974S_Eisenhower_Obverse.jpg/330px-1974S_Eisenhower_Obverse.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/1974S_Eisenhower_Obverse.jpg/440px-1974S_Eisenhower_Obverse.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1400" data-file-height="1395" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Eisenhower_dollar" title="Eisenhower dollar">Eisenhower dollar</a> was the official U.S. dollar coin from 1971 to 1978</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Interstate Highway System is officially known as the "Dwight D. Eisenhower National System of Interstate and Defense Highways" in his honor. It was inspired in part by Eisenhower's own Army experiences in World War II, where he recognized the advantages of the <a href="/wiki/Autobahn" title="Autobahn">autobahn</a> system in Germany.<sup id="cite_ref-archivesIHS_172-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-archivesIHS-172">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup> Commemorative signs reading "Eisenhower Interstate System" and bearing Eisenhower's permanent <a href="/wiki/General_of_the_Army_(United_States)" title="General of the Army (United States)">5-star rank</a> insignia were introduced in 1993 and now are displayed throughout the Interstate System. Several highways are also named for him, including the <a href="/wiki/Interstate_290_(Illinois)" title="Interstate 290 (Illinois)">Eisenhower Expressway</a> (Interstate 290) near Chicago, the <a href="/wiki/Eisenhower_Tunnel" title="Eisenhower Tunnel">Eisenhower Tunnel</a> on <a href="/wiki/Interstate_70" title="Interstate 70">Interstate 70</a> west of <a href="/wiki/Denver" title="Denver">Denver</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Interstate_80_in_California" title="Interstate 80 in California">Interstate 80 in California</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower_School_for_National_Security_and_Resource_Strategy" title="Dwight D. Eisenhower School for National Security and Resource Strategy">Dwight D. Eisenhower School for National Security and Resource Strategy</a> is a senior war college of the Department of Defense's <a href="/wiki/National_Defense_University" title="National Defense University">National Defense University</a> in Washington, DC. Eisenhower graduated from this school when it was previously known as the <a href="/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower_School_for_National_Security_and_Resource_Strategy" title="Dwight D. Eisenhower School for National Security and Resource Strategy">Army Industrial College</a>. 
</p><p>Eisenhower was honored on a <a href="/wiki/Eisenhower_dollar" title="Eisenhower dollar">US one dollar coin</a>, minted from 1971 to 1978. His centenary was honored on the <a href="/wiki/Eisenhower_commemorative_dollar" class="mw-redirect" title="Eisenhower commemorative dollar">Eisenhower commemorative dollar</a> issued in 1990.
</p><p>In 1969 four major record companies&#160;– <a href="/wiki/ABC_Records" title="ABC Records">ABC Records</a>, <a href="/wiki/MGM_Records" title="MGM Records">MGM Records</a>, <a href="/wiki/Buddha_Records" class="mw-redirect" title="Buddha Records">Buddha Records</a> and <a href="/wiki/Caedmon_Audio" title="Caedmon Audio">Caedmon Audio</a>&#160;– released tribute albums in Eisenhower's honor.<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1999, the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Congress" title="United States Congress">United States Congress</a> created the <a href="/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower_Memorial" title="Dwight D. Eisenhower Memorial">Dwight D. Eisenhower Memorial</a> Commission, to create an enduring <a href="/wiki/National_memorial_(United_States)" class="mw-redirect" title="National memorial (United States)">national memorial</a> in Washington, D.C. In 2009 the commission chose the architect <a href="/wiki/Frank_Gehry" title="Frank Gehry">Frank Gehry</a> to design the memorial.<sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-WPmemorial_339-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WPmemorial-339">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup> The groundbreaking ceremony of the memorial was held on November 3, 2017, and was dedicated on September 17, 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-program_341-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-program-341">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup> It stands on a 4-acre (1.6&#160;ha) site near the <a href="/wiki/National_Mall" title="National Mall">National Mall</a> on Maryland Avenue, southwest across the street from the <a href="/wiki/National_Air_and_Space_Museum" title="National Air and Space Museum">National Air and Space Museum</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In December 1999 he was listed on <a href="/wiki/Gallup%27s_List_of_Widely_Admired_People" class="mw-redirect" title="Gallup&#39;s List of Widely Admired People">Gallup's List of Most Widely Admired People of the 20th century</a>. In 2009 he was named to the <a href="/wiki/World_Golf_Hall_of_Fame" title="World Golf Hall of Fame">World Golf Hall of Fame</a> in the Lifetime Achievement category for his contributions to the sport.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup> In 1973, he was inducted into the <a href="/wiki/Hall_of_Great_Westerners" title="Hall of Great Westerners">Hall of Great Westerners</a> of the <a href="/wiki/National_Cowboy_%26_Western_Heritage_Museum" title="National Cowboy &amp; Western Heritage Museum">National Cowboy &amp; Western Heritage Museum</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/The_Naming_Commission" class="mw-redirect" title="The Naming Commission">The Naming Commission</a> has recommended that <a href="/wiki/Fort_Gordon" title="Fort Gordon">Fort Gordon</a> be renamed Fort Eisenhower.<sup id="cite_ref-recommendations_345-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-recommendations-345">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Honors">Honors</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Awards_and_decorations">Awards and decorations</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Orden-Pobeda-Marshal_Vasilevsky.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Orden-Pobeda-Marshal_Vasilevsky.jpg/220px-Orden-Pobeda-Marshal_Vasilevsky.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="209" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Orden-Pobeda-Marshal_Vasilevsky.jpg/330px-Orden-Pobeda-Marshal_Vasilevsky.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Orden-Pobeda-Marshal_Vasilevsky.jpg/440px-Orden-Pobeda-Marshal_Vasilevsky.jpg 2x" data-file-width="500" data-file-height="476" /></a><figcaption>The star of the Soviet <a href="/wiki/Order_of_Victory" title="Order of Victory">Order of Victory</a> awarded to Eisenhower<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>

<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Freedom_of_the_City">Freedom of the City</span></h3>
<p>Eisenhower received the <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_the_City" title="Freedom of the City">Freedom</a> honor from several locations, including:
</p>
<ul><li><span class="flagicon"><span class="mw-image-border" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/England" title="England"><img alt="England" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/be/Flag_of_England.svg/23px-Flag_of_England.svg.png" decoding="async" width="23" height="14" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/be/Flag_of_England.svg/35px-Flag_of_England.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/be/Flag_of_England.svg/46px-Flag_of_England.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="480" /></a></span></span> <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_the_City_of_London" title="Freedom of the City of London">Freedom of the City of London</a> on June 12, 1945<sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-353" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-353">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><span class="flagicon"><span class="mw-image-border" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/Northern_Ireland" title="Northern Ireland"><img alt="Northern Ireland" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Flag_of_Northern_Ireland_%281953%E2%80%931972%29.svg/23px-Flag_of_Northern_Ireland_%281953%E2%80%931972%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="23" height="12" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Flag_of_Northern_Ireland_%281953%E2%80%931972%29.svg/35px-Flag_of_Northern_Ireland_%281953%E2%80%931972%29.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Flag_of_Northern_Ireland_%281953%E2%80%931972%29.svg/46px-Flag_of_Northern_Ireland_%281953%E2%80%931972%29.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="600" data-file-height="300" /></a></span></span> <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_the_City" title="Freedom of the City">Freedom of the City</a> of <a href="/wiki/Belfast" title="Belfast">Belfast</a> on August 24, 1945<sup id="cite_ref-:1_354-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-354">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><span class="flagicon"><span class="mw-image-border" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/Scotland" title="Scotland"><img alt="Scotland" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Flag_of_Scotland.svg/23px-Flag_of_Scotland.svg.png" decoding="async" width="23" height="14" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Flag_of_Scotland.svg/35px-Flag_of_Scotland.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Flag_of_Scotland.svg/46px-Flag_of_Scotland.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="600" /></a></span></span> Freedom of the City of <a href="/wiki/Edinburgh" title="Edinburgh">Edinburgh</a> in 1946<sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><span class="flagicon"><span class="mw-image-border" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/Scotland" title="Scotland"><img alt="Scotland" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Flag_of_Scotland.svg/23px-Flag_of_Scotland.svg.png" decoding="async" width="23" height="14" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Flag_of_Scotland.svg/35px-Flag_of_Scotland.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Flag_of_Scotland.svg/46px-Flag_of_Scotland.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="600" /></a></span></span> Freedom of the Burgh of <a href="/wiki/Maybole" title="Maybole">Maybole</a> in October 1946<sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup></li></ul>
